resources.name: Astoria Film Festival Inc
resources.mission: Astoria Film Festival Inc. is a 501c3 non-profit organization and an official NYC DOE VENDOR, founded by an Astoria-born First-Gen woman with a background in media production and education, that brings filmmaking workshops, film events, film/media workforce training, and film/video production services to the NYC Community, with a focus on empowering aspiring and emerging filmmakers. We provide film education, media production workforce trainings, media career fairs, and festivals
resources.social: Facebook: @astoriafilmfest; Instagram: @astoriafilmfestival; Tik Tok: @astoriafilmfest; YouTube: @astoriafilmfestival; LinkedIn: @astoriafilmfestival

resources.name: Astoria Woodworkers Collective, Inc.
resources.mission: The Astoria Woodworking Collective's mission is to make the craft more accessible to aspiring woodworkers in Queens by providing opportunities and resources to improve their skills and build community. We are an entirely volunteer-run organization, providing shared shop space for members, woodworking classes, and opportunities for volunteers to help us make things for other nonprofit and mission-driven organizations!

resources.name: Dance Entropy Inc.
resources.address: 37-24 24th Street, Floor 2, Suite #212, Long Island City, NY 11101
resources.mission: Our mission is to create a platform for multicultural understanding through dance, nurture connections between dance creation and education, and foster physicality, creativity and empowerment in underserved communities. Dance Entropy Inc. includes Valerie Green/ Dance Entropy and Green Space.

resources.name: Green Space (Dance Entropy Inc.)
resources.address: 37-24 24th Street, Floor 2, Suite 211, Long Island City, NY 11101
resources.mission: As a 24/7 resource, Green Space aims to provide an affordable, welcoming environment for rehearsals, classes, and performance opportunities. We embrace the diversity of Long Island City as an asset, encouraging exchange on an artistic, educational, and interactive level. Dance Entropy Inc. includes both Valerie Green/Dance Entropy and Green Space. Come dance with us!

resources.name: GROOVE NYC Org
resources.mission: GROOVE NYC empowers students, educators, and community leaders by providing them with tailored resources and innovative strategies that help them effectively manage stress, nurture their individuality, and thrive through the transformative power of the healing arts.

resources.name: Hellenic Film Society
resources.mission: The Hellenic Film Society (HFS) is dedicated to promoting Greek cinema throughout the United States. Our mission is to share the richness of Greek films with a wider American audience, to showcase Greek movies, and to preserve the film heritage of Greece. HFS annually presents the New York Greek Film Expo, a Greek film festival for all New Yorkers and also presents Always on Sunday, a monthly Greek film series, both presented in collaboration with the prestigious Museum of the Moving Image in Astoria, Queens.
resources.social: Instagram: @hellenicfilmsociety;; Facebook: @hellenicfilmusa; YouTube: @HellenicFilmSocietyUSA; LinkedIn: @Hellenic Film Society
resources.fees: Most film screenings require purchased tickets.

resources.name: Hour Children, Inc.
resources.mission: Hour Children's mission is to assist incarcerated and formerly incarcerated women and children to successfully rejoin the community, reunify with their families, and build healthy, independent secure lives. To accomplish this Hour Children provides comprehensive services and encourages all to live and interact with dignity and respect. Our vision is to break the cycle of intergenerational incarceration. Hour Children, Inc. also runs a community food pantry, workforce development program and transitional housing.
resources.social: Facebook: @Hour Children Inc; Instagram: @hour_Children; LinkedIn: @Hour Children Inc

resources.name: IndieSpace
resources.mission: IndieSpace celebrates and centers independent theater-making in New York City. We provide radically transparent, responsive and equity-focused funding, real estate programs, professional development, and advocacy to individual artists, theater companies, and indie venues. We are a service organization for artists and cultural workers.

resources.name: Ionian Cultural Federation of America
resources.mission: The Ionian Cultural Federation exists to celebrate and preserve the rich cultural legacy of the Ionian Islands while fostering inclusive artistic dialogue within the diverse communities of New York City. We are committed to bridging heritage and innovation by supporting creative expression, intercultural exchange, and educational initiatives that reflect the needs and aspirations of New Yorkers. Through accessible programming, community partnerships, and cultural advocacy, we aim to empower underrepresented voices, strengthen neighborhood identity, and cultivate a shared sense of belonging rooted in both tradition and transformation.

resources.name: Jacob A. Riis Neighborhood Settlement
resources.mission: Jacob A. Riis Neighborhood Settlement builds and strengthens underserved communities in western Queens and acts as a catalyst for change. We also offer Immigration Services, Older Adult Services, and Youth Programming.

resources.name: Jacob A. Riis Neighborhood Settlement
resources.mission: Jacob A. Riis Neighborhood Settlement is a social services organization that serves youth, families, immigrants, and older adults in Long Island City, Astoria, and the broader western Queens community. Our wide range of offerings includes after-school and summer camp programs for youth (K-12); ESOL classes and legal support for immigrant community members; and recreational activities, meal services, and nursing support for older adults. Our mission is to build and strengthen underserved communities in western Queens and to act as a catalyst for change.

resources.name: Long Island City Partnership
resources.address: 27-01 Queens Plaza North, Level B, LIC, NY 11101
resources.mission: Long Island City Partnership (LICP) champions economic development efforts that benefit the neighborhood at large, along with its members, composed of businesses and organizations reflective of LIC's industrial, commercial, retail, science and technology, residential, cultural, and tourism sectors. LICP works to attract new businesses to LIC, support and sustain existing ones, engage residents and visitors, and promote a vibrant and authentic mixeduse community. LICP also manages the LIC Business Improvement District (LIC BID) and LIC Industrial Business Zone (LIC IBZ), providing business services and assistance.
resources.social: Facebook: @licpartnership; Twitter: @licpartnership; Instagram: @licqns; LinkedIn: @Long Island City Partnership
resources.languages: Services are primarily given in English.
resources.fees: Business Assistance services are free for any business located in Long Island City. Additional programs and services are available to members.

resources.name: Mission to End Modern Slavery (MEMS)
resources.address: 34-18 Northern Blvd, Long Island City, NY 11101
resources.mission: The Mission to End Modern Slavery is a nonprofit organization that empowers migrant workers to lead the movement to end labor trafficking and wage theft. Through capacity building, case management, research, and advocacy, we seek to strengthen migrant workers' ability to organize for social and economic justice.

resources.name: Projekt NYC
resources.mission: Project NYC will enable youth to thrive by empowering them through education, mentorship, and opportunities for personal growth, fostering their potential to become confident leaders and active contributors to their communities for positive change.

resources.name: RGI Alakdan New York, Inc.
resources.mission: To promote brotherhood through community service.

resources.name: Rock Rising, Inc.
resources.mission: Amplify artists. Connect communities. Spark collaboration. Core Values: • Equity: fair pay for artists, free programming for youth • Community-first: created by and for Astoria and Western Queens • Education & Expression: lifelong learning through the arts • Intergenerational impact: centering youth and elders, emerging artists and seasoned professionals. We are opening a physical theater space in 2027 in Astoria at Crescent/Broadway. Our space will be a shared community theater space! We want to spread the word about it!

resources.name: The Chocolate Factory Theater
resources.mission: Founded in 2004, The Chocolate Factory Theater (CF) supports the creation of new work by interdisciplinary performance artists from its post-industrial facility in Long Island City, Queens. We encourage risk-taking and innovation within the experimental performing arts community by responding to artists' needs with space, time, money and administrative support throughout their careers. As an artist-founded, artist-run institution-and one of the few remaining spaces wholly devoted to experimental performance in New York City-we believe that the ideas generated within our walls have the potential to improve the lives of New Yorkers, shape broader cultural movements, and inspire change.

resources.name: The Steven Spectrum Career Project
resources.mission: Our mission is to empower the neurodivergent community by providing the skills and support needed to overcome employment challenges. We envision a future where neurodiversity is embraced, and everyone has equal opportunities to succeed in their chosen careers. We believe in the power of diversity and the strength of inclusion.

resources.name: Urban Upbound
resources.mission: Urban Upbound provides low-income New Yorkers the tools and resources needed to achieve economic mobility and self sufficiency.

resources.name: Witness to Mass Incarceration
resources.address: 36-46 37th Street, Second Floor, Long Island City, NY 11101
resources.mission: Witness to Mass Incarceration (WITNESS) is dedicated to fostering economic independence for formerly incarcerated (FIP), system-impacted, LGBTQ+ individuals and the migrant community. We achieve this by building a hub of excellence in entrepreneurship and innovation, offering comprehensive vocational training, social enterprise solutions, and robust support systems. Our mission is to cultivate economic independence, reduce recidivism, and nurture generational wealth, while dismantling systemic barriers and advancing equality for all we serve.

resources.name: Young Invincibles
resources.mission: Our mission is to amplify the voices of young adults in the political process and expand economic opportunity for our generations. Our issue areas are healthcare, higher education, workforce development, and civic engagement. We work with young adults, ages 18-34, especially college students, graduate students, and folks from working class/ low-income and marginalized backgrounds to ensure we all have a seat at the table and input on economic issues that impact our finances, our health, and our futures. We do issue-based organizing, research, storytelling, and advocacy. Info about our young adult (18-34 years old) engagement programs can be found here: younginvincibles.org/youth-engagement-programs
